chapters.1: Nahum opens by declaring that God is slow to anger but will not let evil go unpunished, and that his power is seen in storms, earthquakes, and nature itself. He announces that Nineveh, capital of Assyria, is about to be completely destroyed, while Judah will finally have relief from its oppressor.
chapters.2: This chapter vividly pictures the siege and fall of Nineveh: chariots racing through the streets, gates thrown open, the city's treasures plundered, and its people fleeing in panic. The once-mighty city, compared to a lion's den full of prey, is left empty and ruined.
chapters.3: Nahum condemns Nineveh as a bloody, deceitful city built on violence and exploitation of other nations. He describes its coming total collapse in humiliating detail, comparing its many officials to locusts that will simply fly away, leaving no one to mourn its destruction.
